vibemathed.name: YAH mixed-base Collatz system: scalar arctic first-step obstruction
vibemathed.statement: Yolcu, Aaronson and Heule (2023, section 6) raise whether suitable matrix interpretations might fail to establish termination of their mixed-base Collatz rewrite system. This broad direction remains open. The restricted subquestion here is whether any standard coefficientwise dimension-one arctic-natural interpretation, with unbounded nonnegative finite coefficients, can weakly orient all eleven rules and strictly orient a nonempty first full rule-removal subset, a boundary-rule subset in the original relative-top orientation, or a dynamic-rule subset in the reversed relative-top orientation. The fixed two-state twenty-two-rule labeling is also considered. The exact scalar subquestion was not separately posed in the cited paper.

vibemathed.verificationNote: The complete YAH full-plus-top obstruction is supported by prose soundness arguments and replayable exact Python certificates, not a complete Lean proof. Internal semantic review found no defect: 288,560 differential assignments, 491 Farkas identities, 426 RUP clauses and ten terminal contradictions passed. Finite diagnostics are not the unrestricted proof; the interpretation-to-formula argument plus exact refutations cover unbounded coefficients. There is no external referee endorsement or independent priority certification. The consolidated archive separately contains Lean-checked Collatz auxiliary results; their build and axiom audits do not transfer Lean status to this YAH claim.
vibemathed.field: Term rewriting; proof-method limitations; Collatz dynamics
vibemathed.resultNote: No first standard coefficientwise dimension-one arctic-natural step exists for the eleven-rule YAH system in full/extended mode or either specified relative-top opportunity. A fixed two-state twenty-two-rule labeling satisfies the corresponding syntactic exclusions; equal-label lifting gives the original-system result. The coefficient domain is unbounded. Full mode uses positive cancellation; ten top cases use exact Farkas/RUP refutations. The original full scalar argument is elementary and uses established weight techniques. The combined top/labeled exclusion is the candidate contribution: no exact prior match was located in a bounded review. Higher dimensions, other carriers or labelings, other orders and transformations, later scalar steps, and Collatz convergence remain outside the result.
